title: Hall Sausage Biscuits & Gravy
subtitle: Flaky biscuits split and smothered in peppery sausage gravy for twelve.
description: Classic hall comfort: bulk breakfast sausage gravy thick enough to coat a spoon, ladled over split baking-powder biscuits. Uses shortcut biscuits from the oven so the cook focuses on gravy that stays smooth and seasoned while feeding a full shift.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.notes: freshly ground, plus salt to taste

ingredients.name: chopped parsley
ingredients.notes: and hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Hall Sausage Biscuits & Gravy in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Bake the biscuits
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Arrange biscuits on a sheet pan and brush tops with melted butter. Bake until golden and cooked through—split one to check the center isn't doughy. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: In a large Dutch oven or deep skillet, brown sausage over medium-high, breaking it into fine crumbles. Don't drain all the fat—you need it for the roux. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale.

steps.title: Build the roux
steps.instruction: Sprinkle flour over the sausage and fat, stirring constantly for 1–2 minutes until the raw flour smell cooks off and the mixture looks sandy. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Whisk in milk
steps.instruction: Add warm milk gradually, whisking to prevent lumps. Simmer until gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. Season aggressively with black pepper and salt. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Split and ladle
steps.instruction: Split warm biscuits and place two halves per bowl or plate. Ladle hot gravy over the top until generously covered. Garnish with parsley and serve immediately. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Warm milk in a microwave or small pot before whisking—cold milk shocks the roux and causes lumps.
Hold biscuits uncovered at 200°F while gravy finishes; covered biscuits steam soft tops.
Keep gravy on the lowest simmer with a ladle in the pot at the line for second portions.
cleanupNotes: Fill the gravy pot with hot soapy water immediately—flour-milk paste sets hard within minutes.
Discard any biscuit crumbs on the sheet pan before they bake onto the metal during cleanup.
leftovers: Gravy reheats smoothly with extra milk over low heat; thin until pourable before ladling.
Split leftover biscuits and griddle cut-side down, then top with reheated gravy and a fried egg.
